# JustSearch

> Local-first neural search for your personal files.

## Canonical vs noncanonical (critical)

- **Canonical (must not drift):** `docs/explanation/`, `docs/reference/`, `docs/how-to/`, `docs/decisions/`
- **Noncanonical (allowed to drift):** `docs/tempdocs/`, `docs/future-features/` (and background folders like `docs/Hardware/`, `docs/Economy/`)
- **Design contracts (dated, per lane):** `docs/design/<lane>/` holds a locked design plus its verified code facts, evidence and stage checklists (for example `docs/design/lane-f-engine-jvm/`). Not a tempdoc (no size cap, no append-only convention) and not canonical (`docs-validate` does not cover it); its status line and section 0 say what is decided.

If docs disagree, treat **canonical** docs as truth. If canonical docs are unclear, verify against code + contract tests.

This repo does not maintain an `llms-full.txt`. Use this file as the index and follow links into canonical docs.

## Summary
JustSearch runs entirely on localhost. Since ADR-0049 it is **one JVM plus two process boundaries**:
1.  **Engine:** the API gateway and the index half (Lucene, Tika extraction) in a single JVM. The
    two halves are a module boundary reached through ports, not a process boundary.
2.  **Brain (Inference):** a separate `llama-server` process for RAG and Chat — a different runtime
    and toolchain, which is why it stays out of process.
3.  **Extraction sandbox pool:** child JVMs that parse untrusted files (ADR-0048), so a parser
    crash or hang cannot take the Engine down.

We strictly enforce "Inversion of Control" for configuration. There is no memory-mapped IPC: the
halves share objects.

- [Process Coordination](explanation/02-process-coordination.md): How the Engine coordinates its in-process owners, native children, host supervision, signalling, and ordered shutdown.
- [Knowledge Server](explanation/03-knowledge-server.md): Formatting logic, JobQueue, and Tika usage.
- [Storage Engine](explanation/04-storage-engine.md): Lucene internals, schema (SSOT), and locking strategies.
- [AI Architecture](explanation/05-ai-architecture.md): Hybrid Inference (CPU/GPU) and VRAM management.
- [Configuration & SSOT](explanation/06-configuration-ssot.md): The `EnvRegistry` and "Gatekeeper" pattern.
- [UI Host Architecture](explanation/07-ui-host-architecture.md): HeadlessApp, Lit shell-v0 structure, and Auto-Discovery.
- [Observability & Telemetry](explanation/08-observability.md): Telemetry, NDJSON logs, and Distributed Tracing.
- [Testing Strategy](explanation/09-testing-strategy.md): The 4-tier Test Pyramid, Chaos testing, and AI Judge.
- [UI/UX Design System](explanation/10-ui-ux-design.md): The 5-zone layout, interaction model, and design pillars.
- [Index Schema Migration (Blue/Green)](explanation/11-index-schema-migration.md): Blue/green migration mechanics and safety guarantees.
- [Desktop Installer + Sandbox Setup (How it works today)](explanation/12-desktop-installer-and-sandbox-setup.md): NSIS installer, Tauri boot sequence, sandbox harness scripts.
- [AI Setup + Verification (Current State)](explanation/13-ai-setup-and-verification.md): Current v1 setup, installer bundling, and verification workflows.
- [Adapters-Lucene Deep Dive](explanation/18-adapters-lucene-deep-dive.md): HNSW search, SPLADE learned sparse retrieval, hybrid fusion, commit metadata system.
- [Module Architecture & Dependency Governance](explanation/19-module-architecture.md): The Engine's three rings, composition root, Gradle modules, ports, and dependency enforcement.
- [Benchmarking Architecture (Claims + Competitor Suite)](explanation/20-benchmarking-architecture.md): Retired claim/competitor harnesses and the surviving Java benchmarks and jseval tooling.
- [Agent Analytics Pipeline](explanation/21-agent-analytics-pipeline.md): Behavioral tracking pipeline for session and cost analysis and LLM-as-judge evaluation. The hook, skill-delivery, dashboard and process-hygiene scoring layers are retired.
- [Agent System Architecture](explanation/22-agent-system-architecture.md): Agent loop, operation-substrate tool dispatch, token budget, durability, and MCP tool surface.
- [23-runtime-manifest](explanation/23-runtime-manifest.md): Producer-published runtime manifest at <dataDir>/runtime/manifest.json and GET /api/runtime/manifest, projected from the Engine component registry.
- [Search Pipeline Overview](explanation/23-search-pipeline-overview.md): End-to-end search pipeline: ingestion stages, query-time retrieval legs, fusion, correction, reranking, and response assembly.
- [Engine Inference Composition](explanation/24-engine-inference-composition.md): How the Engine resolves installed model inputs, builds ORT sessions, and owns index and query inference generations.
- [Service Lifecycle Pattern](explanation/25-service-lifecycle-pattern.md): Canonical pattern for long-lived resource owners in JustSearch. Identity is held by the consumer; each open period is a single-shot phase value with a clean AutoCloseable lifecycle. Restart is a consumer pattern (build new value, swap holder field, close old) — not a method on the value. Two forms: phase-typed (Form A) when multiple operating modes warrant compile-time distinction, single-shot single-class (Form B) when there's only one mode.
- [The Extension Substrate](explanation/26-extension-substrate.md): How JustSearch is extended: one declaration model, one composer, four shared substrates, the host-owns-truth boundary, and trust-proportional isolation — the invariants every contributor (plugin, operation, resource, prompt, MCP tool, workflow, agent tool) shares.
- [The Frontend Presentation Kernel](explanation/27-frontend-presentation-kernel.md): How the web frontend prevents presentation drift: single presentation authorities (tone, originator, layout, modality), a closed atom vocabulary, runtime-modality primitives, and catalog-projected gates — the Collapse > Generate > Gate prevention ladder that makes a re-authored badge/modal/transient unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.
- [28-runtime-contract](explanation/28-runtime-contract.md): The JustSearch Runtime Contract — the small, versioned local surface external AI agents target. Public center = the local runtime; the desktop app is its first-party reference client. Defines the v1 stable core (health/status lifecycle subset + MCP endpoint/tools + runtime manifest), discovered through the manifest's runtimeContract descriptor. Matrix + policy + surface classification live in docs/reference/runtime-contract.md.

### How-To (Specific Tasks)
- [Capture UI Evidence](how-to/capture-ui-evidence.md): Screenshot capture for UI verification and agent visual feedback.
- [Developing the UI](how-to/develop-ui.md): Layout work without a backend, deterministic fixture captures, real backend development, and frontend verification.
- [Interpret `jseval bisect` Output (LR5-d)](how-to/interpret-bisect-output.md): Reading the manifest-hash bisection report — single-axis, multi-axis, MULTI_AXIS_INTERACTION, no-cached-run, and identical-cohort paths.
- [Prevent public credential and email exposure](how-to/prevent-public-credential-and-email-exposure.md): Signing diagnostics, secret-scan coverage, commit identity checks, and historical cleanup limits.
- [Spawn an Isolated Test Backend](how-to/spawn-isolated-test-backend.md): Lite mode env flag (JUSTSEARCH_LITE_MODE) and the per-class IsolatedBackendFixture pattern for integration tests that need a clean backend per test class without paying the 3-8s cost of loading the AI stack.
- [Test GPU Inference Locally](how-to/test-gpu-locally.md): How to run llama-server with GPU offload for local development and testing.
- [Using the UI](how-to/use-ui.md): Running dev modes and accessing debug dashboards.
- [Verify an Update Preserves the User's Models](how-to/verify-update-preserves-models.md): Run the Update Preserves Models CI lane, which installs a published release, seeds model files, upgrades to the next release, and asserts the seeded bytes survive both the upgrade and the uninstall.
- [Verify your JustSearch download](how-to/verify-your-download.md): Checking the installer's SHA-256 and Authenticode identity, understanding Windows reputation warnings, and using the build-from-source alternative.
- [Writing a JustSearch plugin](how-to/write-a-plugin.md): Author a V1.5 plugin that runs in a SES Compartment, contributes a Surface, and integrates with the host's trust + capability model.

### Governance (Policies & SLOs)

### Decisions (Architecture Decision Records)
- [Architecture Decision Records](decisions/README.md): Index of architectural decisions with MADR-lite template.
- [ADR-0003: Use Lucene Directly Without Search Platform](decisions/0003-direct-lucene-no-elasticsearch.md): Interact with Lucene API directly instead of Elasticsearch or Solr.
- [ADR-0006: Two-Pronged Citation Strategy](decisions/0006-two-pronged-citation-strategy.md): LLM-generated citations with CPU cross-encoder verification; in grounded answers with a known source list, source labels without verifier backing are removed.
- [ADR-0007: Entity Faceting Over Full Knowledge Graph](decisions/0007-entity-faceting-over-knowledge-graph.md): Selective adoption of NER entity extraction for Lucene keyword facets with SQLite sidecar disambiguation, deferring full knowledge graph.
- [ADR-0008: Settings Are Ephemeral, Defaults Are Safe](decisions/0008-settings-ephemeral-defaults-safe.md): Settings are versioned and forward-migrated. An unreadable file is preserved as a timestamped .corrupt- sibling, replaced with defaults, and surfaced as a lifecycle condition; a newer schemaVersion refuses to load. Owner review of the original ephemeral-settings decision remains open.
- [ADR-0013: Synonyms FST Placeholder](decisions/0013-synonyms-fst-placeholder.md): The synonym FST placeholder is moot: per-language synonyms, SynonymsCompiler and ssotCompileSynonyms were removed (ADR-0043). The live part is the analyzer fingerprinting algorithm: SHA-256 over a sorted-key JSON descriptor, pinned by SsotValidatorFingerprintTest.
- [ADR-0014: Pipeline Definition and Schema Removal](decisions/0014-pipeline-definition-removal.md): Remove pipeline DAG definitions, budget profiles, and pipeline-schema module.
- [ADR-0015: MCP Tool Surface Design](decisions/0015-mcp-tool-surface-design.md): Keep a short task-oriented MCP surface; the accepted seven-tool list includes a read-only operation outcome query for recovery (amended 2026-09-13).
- [ADR-0016: Query Understanding Soft-Boost](decisions/0016-query-understanding-soft-boost.md): Use soft boosts (SHOULD clauses) for QU-extracted signals, not hard filters.
- [ADR-0017: ai-bridge Module Decomposition](decisions/0017-ai-bridge-module-decomposition.md): Split ai-bridge monolith into ai-backend, gpu-bridge, and prompt-support; delete hollow app-ai and unused ai-worker.
- [ADR-0018: VLM PDF Extraction via Chat Model](decisions/0018-vlm-pdf-extraction-via-chat-model.md): Reuse the chat model's vision path, without a Docling sidecar, for visual extraction of PDFs and images; on by default as the second fallback tier.
- [ADR-0019: CPU vs GPU Model Selection Strategy](decisions/0019-cpu-gpu-model-selection-strategy.md): Ship separate FP32 ONNX models for CPU use; use model_manifest.json to select CPU vs GPU variants at runtime.
- [ADR-0020: Structured Metadata Fields as Filterable Facets](decisions/0020-structured-metadata-filterable-facets.md): Extend entity faceting to structured metadata with meta_ prefix, typed proto fields, and two-stage chunk retrieval.
- [ADR-0021: Build-Stamp Content-Hash Design](decisions/0021-build-stamp-content-hash.md): The Engine distribution content hash is generated, but normal startup does not inject it into the running JVM; hot reload sets it. The dev-runner uses a separate mtime-based head stamp for startup freshness. Owner review of the content-hash startup gap remains open.
- [ADR-0022: RecordBuilder Annotation Processor for API Records](decisions/0022-recordbuilder-annotation-processor.md): Use io.soabase record-builder v52 to generate fluent builders for Java records in app-api, enabling additive field evolution.
- [ADR-0023: API Responses Declare Runtime Context](decisions/0023-api-responses-declare-runtime-context.md): Any endpoint whose behavior varies by runtime mode must surface that mode in its response to prevent silent behavioral switches.
- [ADR-0024: App Packaging: NSIS, Per-User Install, Download-on-Demand](decisions/0024-app-packaging-nsis-per-user-download.md): Use NSIS installer with per-user install to LocalAppData and post-install model download via Install AI flow.
- [ADR-0025: Core DTO Dual-Type Layering (in-process ports vs REST)](decisions/0025-core-dto-dual-type-layering.md): Maintain separate core DTOs for in-process ports and app-api records for REST as intentional layering, not duplication.
- [ADR-0026: Manual-Only CI Triggering](decisions/0026-manual-ci-triggering.md): Manual-only workflow policy for the former self-hosted/local-runner model; ADR-0044 narrows it for public hosted CI and ADR-0052 schedules CodeQL weekly while keeping manual dispatch.
- [ADR-0027: MetricCatalog as the Telemetry Contract](decisions/0027-metric-catalog-as-telemetry-contract.md): MetricCatalog is the typed telemetry contract; the legacy Telemetry emission surface is retired. Two KnowledgeSearchEngine skip counters still bypass the catalog through GlobalOpenTelemetry, as recorded in the 2026-10-20 amendment.
- [ADR-0028: Scoped Reverse Path-Hash Lookup](decisions/0028-scoped-reverse-path-lookup.md): Refines the tempdoc-410 ingestion-ledger privacy contract. Raw paths still never appear in any operator-visible export, telemetry stream, or support-bundle generation. They may now be returned by a single index call (originally a Worker RPC, now the in-process `IngestServiceCalls#lookupPathByHash`) reachable only from one HTTP endpoint, invoked in direct response to a user's 'show filename' click in the local UI. Backed by an internal-only `path_resolution` table and an ArchUnit guard.
- [ADR-0029: TelemetryEvents Bridge vs Direct-Emit Façade for MetricCatalog Adoption](decisions/0029-telemetry-events-bridge-vs-direct-emit.md): Each MetricCatalog adoption picks between two consumption idioms — a TelemetryEvents bridge interface (decouples domain code from telemetry types; required when the domain module should not depend on the catalog package) or a direct-emit façade that wraps catalog instruments (cheaper when the domain module already depends on the catalog package). The choice is module-dep-driven, not preference-driven. Five shipped instances codify the criteria.
- [ADR-0030: Policy on Operations vs MCP-style hints — JustSearch's deliberate divergence](decisions/0030-policy-on-operations-vs-mcp-hints.md): JustSearch's Operation registry primitive carries enforced policy fields (risk, confirm, audit, retry, required capabilities) on the entry, while MCP keeps equivalent metadata as untrusted hints clients should not trust. The divergence is justified by JustSearch's single-trust-domain threat model. MCP discipline is reserved for untrusted plugins via a trust-tier-aware executor whose untrusted branch is not implemented yet; rateLimit was removed (amended 2026-08-26).
- [ADR-0031: Frontend three primitives — Operation, Resource, Prompt](decisions/0031-fe-three-primitives.md): The frontend framework is built on backend-declared registry primitives — originally three, Operation (do), Resource (observe), Prompt (ask), mirroring the MCP split, and now four with DiagnosticChannel. All UI affordances project from these.
- [ADR-0032: Frontend rendering — Lit web components](decisions/0032-fe-lit-web-components.md): The frontend is authored as Lit web components; the React stack was retired in the rewrite.
- [ADR-0033: Frontend as a framework, not a product](decisions/0033-fe-framework-not-product.md): The frontend kernel docs define a framework, not the final product UX; product UX commitments stay out of docs/reference/ui/frontend-kernel/kernel/.
- [ADR-0034: Backend-owned truth — the frontend renders, never owns](decisions/0034-fe-backend-owned-truth.md): Operations, Resources, and Prompts (the truth) are singular and backend-owned; the frontend is a renderer/composition layer over them.
- [ADR-0035: Plugin boundary — truth vs presentation](decisions/0035-fe-plugin-boundary.md): Plugins extend presentation while core backend truth remains backend-owned. The frontend Resource overlay still permits colliding plugin IDs to replace catalog entries; the intended boundary is not fully enforced by types.
- [ADR-0036: Resource Category axis](decisions/0036-fe-resource-category.md): Resource is one primitive with a typed Category axis (STATE, EVENT_STREAM, HISTORY, TABULAR, TIMESERIES) rather than a primitive per kind, so new information shapes are typed values, not new primitives.
- [ADR-0037: Universal SSE envelope](decisions/0037-universal-sse-envelope.md): Streaming Resources share one SSE envelope (event frame: a LIFECYCLE snapshot followed by UPDATE frames); chat and agent run streams are outside this envelope contract.
- [ADR-0038: Wire contract as a first-class artifact](decisions/0038-wire-contract-source-of-truth.md): The FE↔backend wire contract is a first-class, versioned artifact with one authority (since tempdoc 564, the Java record); hand-written per-language mirrors are forbidden and consumer-side types are meant to be generated from it. Migration is incomplete: named mirrors remain as declared exceptions (amended 2026-09-02), and the probe cannot see unmarked ones.
- [ADR-0039: Contract substrate — every published contract is a first-class artifact](decisions/0039-contract-substrate.md): One authority per contract Category, projected per target; only wire is registered. Tempdoc 564 supersedes the proto-as-source realization for frontend wire types: Java records drive JSON Schema and TS/Zod projection.
- [ADR-0042: Live-registry witness — consumer-presence over the live ContributionRegistry](decisions/0042-runtime-witness-consumer-presence.md): A delivered contribution must carry a consumer, checked by LiveWitnessTest over the live ContributionRegistry, covering runtime-composed MCP and plugin contributions the static snapshot cannot see; core workflow operations are included in the static snapshot.
- [ADR-0043: Multilingual by construction — no per-language levers](decisions/0043-multilingual-by-construction-no-per-language-levers.md): Retrieval analysis uses one multilingual model stack and locale-invariant analysis, with no per-language stemmers, analyzer fields, spelling dictionaries or curated synonyms. English word lists remain in NER cleanup; the 2026-10-20 amendment records this limit of the broader engine claim.
- [ADR-0044: Public hosted CI fact lanes](decisions/0044-public-hosted-ci-fact-lanes.md): The public repository runs standard GitHub-hosted CI on push and pull requests, split into stable fact lanes; self-hosted and specialty workflows remain manually dispatched unless separately amended.
- [ADR-0045: Public main history publication](decisions/0045-public-main-history-publication.md): Public main receives curated squash commits from pull requests while branch commits remain workspace history.
- [ADR-0046: Local API trust boundary](decisions/0046-local-api-trust-boundary.md): The local HTTP API's trust boundary is the owning OS user: an owner-only credential file and authentication on every non-public production route, alongside loopback bind, Host allowlist, MCP Origin validation and desktop CORS.
- [ADR-0047: Context window is a derived resource](decisions/0047-context-window-is-a-derived-resource.md): The LLM context window is derived at activation from a ladder of explicit rungs (up to 32k on GPU, capped by the per-card profile; 8k on CPU; stepped down on a launch abort) rather than configured as a user preference, and every prompt-side budget is a fraction of the live window rather than a constant.
- [ADR-0048: Extraction isolation and indexing pacing](decisions/0048-extraction-isolation-and-indexing-pacing.md): Untrusted parsing runs in a persistent child process pool rather than in the Engine JVM; foreground contention is answered with a duty cycle rather than a pause; Engine health is sampled internally rather than on the request thread; ingestion failures walk a bounded retry ladder to a visible terminal state; and NRT/commit cadence is decided by measurement, which rejected the first candidate.
- [ADR-0049: One Engine JVM, and the process boundaries that survive](decisions/0049-one-engine-jvm-and-the-boundaries-that-survive.md): The application half and the index half share one JVM and meet at catalogued ports; the boundaries that remain are llama-server and the extraction child pool, each justified by a differing runtime, failure domain or scarce resource.
- [ADR-0050: GPU co-residence by prevention, measured profiles and explicit degradation](decisions/0050-gpu-co-residence-by-prevention.md): The chat model and the ONNX encoders share one consumer GPU by not overlapping bulk GPU work with chat generation or a foreground game, by fixed per-card profiles built from measured and capped footprints, and by unloading the chat model under external pressure; a search that cannot get semantic results in time returns keyword results with a reason instead of timing out.
- [ADR-0051: Held process lifetimes and owner-recorded exits](decisions/0051-held-process-lifetimes-and-owner-exit-records.md): Every service process is bound to its owner's lifetime, so nothing outlives the process that started it: on Windows through the owner's kill-on-close job, on Linux through PR_SET_PDEATHSIG set by the bound-exec helper. The chat server is no longer adopted across Engine restarts; every stop is recorded by its owner with a reason before it happens, and instruments classify exits from those records instead of from exit codes.
- [ADR-0052: Weekly CodeQL on hosted runners](decisions/0052-weekly-codeql-on-hosted-runners.md): CodeQL code scanning runs weekly on GitHub-hosted runners and stays dispatchable by hand; it is advisory and never gates a merge.

<!-- generated:end -->

## Core Concepts

*   **SSOT (Single Source of Truth):** We define schema in JSON, not code.
*   **Zero-Shared-Nothing:** Application code *never* touches Lucene files — index I/O belongs to
    the index half, reached through a port (hard invariant 1, ADR-0049).
*   **No internal wire:** the internal transport is retired; there is no gRPC server and no port to discover. The index half is bound
    in-process by `EngineRoot`; only the Brain is reached over a socket.
*   **Local-only HTTP:** The Local API binds to loopback (`127.0.0.1`). The UI resolves its port from a URL/env override, the host (Tauri shell or bridge), or the Vite dev proxy (`resolveApiEndpoint` in `modules/ui-web/src/api/http.ts`); it does not probe ports.
